contexts.text: The second birth of the Church is charity, which is signified by Abel and brother. AC 342. AC 366.

That charity is the brother of faith, may be evident to everyone from the nature or essence of faith; their brotherhood was represented by Esau and Jacob, wherefore there was strife concerning the primogeniture...
The union of charity and faith is signified by the covenant of brethren ().
They were called brethren by the Lord who hear the Word and do it. (). They who hear are they who have faith; they who do are they who have charity.

At the hand of a man's brother () = from the whole of his Intellectual... The Intellectual with man is called a man a brother; whether it be a true Intellectual, a spurious Intellectual, or a false Intellectual, it is still called a man a brother; for the understanding is called a man and the brother of the will...
They are called his brothers () because he professed faith, (for) charity is the brother of faith. AC 1091:end.
Lot his brother's son () = sensuous truth... Brother also = the truth of faith, thus here, sensuous truth. See AC 1707:end.
In Heaven they do not know what a brother is, except from such brotherhood as there is in Heaven.
We are men brethren () = that in themselves they are united. Men brethren = union, and in fact the union of truth and good. AC 1594.
All the sons of the primitive Church lived together as brethren, and also called each other brethren.
Hatred is described by no man shall spare his brother ().
He shall dwell against the faces of all his brethren () = that there will be continual contentions about the things of faith, but still he will be the victor. AC 3277.
(Meeting in the Spiritual World of two brothers, one of whom had died in infancy.)

The reason Lot called (the Sodomites) brethren () was that he exhorted them from what was good. In the Word, brother has the same signification as neighbour, for this reason, that everyone should love his neighbour as himself; thus brethren are so called from love, or what is the same, from good... In Heaven the Lord is the Father of all... Hence all the Sons of Israel, representing the heavenly kingdom of the Lord, that is, the kingdom of love and charity, were called the brethren and also the companions, of each other. Illustrated.
Brethren = all who are in good.

Hence it follows that all in the universe are called brethren who are the neighbour, and this because everyone ought to love his neighbour as himself, thus from love or good; and as the Lord is good itself, and regards all from good, and is Himself the neighbour in the highest sense, He also calls them brethren. Illustrated. Hence it is evident that brother is a term of love.
This is my brother, I see that he worships the Lord, and is a good man.
Under Sister, see this reference.
Brother () = the good of truth. AC 2563.
Brother () = celestial good adjoined to rational truth as a brother to a sister.
They who are in brotherhood from good...
The Angels consider man as a brother...
Under Charity, see this reference.
Under House, see this reference, and at AC 3128.
The brother of Rebekah () = the affection of good in the natural man... In the Word, brother = the affection of good, and sister, the affection of truth.
He gave precious things to her brother () = spiritual things for natural good... Brother = natural good.

And afterwards his brother went forth () = truth. Brother = good and also truth, which are here called brothers. As charity is the brother of faith, or good the brother of truth, so on the other hand, is faith the brother of charity, or truth the brother of good; also, in the Natural, the affection of good is called brother, and the affection of truth sister...
They swore a man to his brother () = confirmation with those who are in the good of truth... Man with brother = the good of truth, or those who are in that good; man = truth, and brother, good.

Be master over thy brethren () = at first an apparent dominion of the affection of natural truth over the affections of natural good... Brethren = the affections of good, here of the Natural. AC 3597:4.
A man shall take hold of his brother in the house of his father () = to acknowledge anything for good.
My brethren, whence are you? () = from what origin is charity there. Brethren = those who are in good, and thence good itself, thus charity.
Brother, who here is Jacob () = good. References.

The reason Jacob called himself the brother of Laban, when yet he was the son of his sister, is that all are brethren from good, and hence also Laban in turn calls Jacob his brother; for it is good which produces consanguinity and which conjoins, for good is of love, and love is spiritual conjunction. Hence it was that in the ancient Churches all those who were in good were called brethren; and also in the Jewish Church... but in this Church only those who were born Jews. The primitive Christian Church also called all brethren who were in good, but afterwards only those who were in their own congregation. But among Christians, the name brother vanished together with good, and when truth succeeded in the place of good, or faith in the place of charity, they could no longer call each other brethren from good, but the neighbour. The doctrine of faith without the life of charity has also this in it, that brotherhood with one who is lower than themselves seems to be beneath them; for brotherhood does not derive its origin with them from the Lord and thus from good, but from themselves, and thus from honours and gain.

And Laban said to Jacob, Because thou art my brother () = because they are blood relations from good... Brother = good, here consanguinity, because it is said by Laban to Jacob, thus by good to good for all consanguinity derives its origin from good, for good is of love. It is the nearest degree of love in the line of descent which is called consanguinity, and is meant in the proper sense by brother.

(Laban) took his brethren with him () = goods in place of those which he had lost. Brethren = goods. References. In the inward sense, by brethren are signified those who are in similar good and truth, that is, in a similar affection of good and truth; for in the other life all are consociated according to affections, and they who are consociated constitute a brotherhood; not that they call themselves brethren, but that they are brethren through conjunction. In the other life good and truth themselves constitute that which on earth is called relationship by blood and by marriage. Explained. AC 4129.
My brethren and thy brethren () = what is just and fair. Explained. Brethren = goods.

Jacob said to his brethren () = those who are in the good of works. Brethren = goods, here, those who are in the goods of works, who are the gentiles; for all who are in good are conjoined with the Divine of the Lord, and on account of that conjunction are called by the Lord brethren. Illustrated. AE 746:10, Illustrated.

He called his brethren to eat bread () = the appropriation of good from the Lord's Divine Natural. Brethren = those who were now conjoined in a covenant, that is, in friendship; and in the inward sense, those who are in good and truth. References. AC 4239. AC 4247. AC 4267.
Under Good, see this reference.
Brethren, here the sons of Israel () = truths.
Dinah's brethren () = the truths and goods of that Church. Brethren = truths and goods, or faith and charity.
Simeon and Levi... are called brethren (), because good is the brother of truth, or charity of faith.

(Joseph) was pasturing the flock with his brethren () = that it was among those who being in faith were teaching... In this chapter, brethren = the Church which is turning away from charity to faith, and at last to faith separated, and thus to falsities. AC 4679. AC 4721. AC 4740. AC 4754.
His brethren saw () = those things which are of faith, and in the proximate sense, the descendants of Jacob. AC 4680. AC 4683.
He told his brethren () = before those who are in faith separate. AC 4694.

The father and brethren of Joseph, here = the Jewish religion from the ancient one... Its external together with its internal is what is here called father, and its external without an internal, brethren. Hence it is said that his brethren envied him, but his father kept the word, and by these words is signified the aversion of those who are in what is external without what is internal, but that the Truth still remained in their religiosity. Explained. AC 4702.
Go, see the peace of the brethren () = every advent of the Lord, and perception how it was with those who are teaching... Brethren, here = those who are teaching from faith.

A man to his brother () = mutually. A man to his brother was the customary formula with the ancients when what was mutual was meant, because a man = truth, and a brother good, between which there exists the veriest mutuality itself...

Joseph's brethren = those within the Church who confirm themselves against Divine truth, especially against these two things, that the Lord's Human is Divine, and that the works of charity contribute to salvation; and this not only in doctrine, but also in life.
Judah said to his brethren () = the depraved in the Church who are against all good whatever... His brethren = those in the Church who are in faith separate.
For he is our brother and our flesh () = because what is from them is accepted. Brother = what is consanguineous from good.
(Reuben) returned to his brethren () = those who teach. The brethren of Joseph = those who are in faith separate, and as they were shepherds, they also = those who teach from faith.
A brother represented consanguineous good with which there is to be conjoined the truth which was represented by his widow...
Behold, his brother came out () = the truth of good, brother = what is consanguineous from good, thus the truth of good. Explained.
My brethren () = those who are in the good of charity and of life, for the Lord is with them, because they are in good itself, and they are those who are properly meant by the neighbour...
Brethren = the goods which are of charity. References.

Joseph's ten brethren () = such truths of the Church as corresponded. Brethren = the truths which are of the Church; these are here called the brethren of Joseph, who = truth from the Divine, from correspondence; for the correspondence causes them to be conjoined as a brother with a brother. Explained.
Joseph's brethren came () = the general truths of the Church without mediation. Explained. AC 5421. AC 5427.

We thy servants are twelve brethren () = that all things of faith are thus conjoined together... Brethren = conjunction through good; for when truths are conjoined through good, they put on as it were a brotherhood among each other...

Benjamin his brother, the son of his mother () = the internal from the Natural as from a mother... Everyone is called a brother by the Lord... who has anything of the good of charity from the Lord. AC 5692.
Thy father and thy brethren... meaning Israel and his sons () = spiritual good from the Natural, and the truths of the Church therein. AC 6102. AC 6106.

Thy brethren shall celebrate thee () = that this Church is pre-eminent above the rest... Brethren = the truths which are of this Church, thus also the Churches which are in the truths which are represented by Judah's brethren, for truths and goods constitute the Church. The truths of the celestial Church are signified by thy brethren, or those of Judah; and the truths of the spiritual Church, by the sons of his father.

His brethren () = truths thence derived, (for) the sons of Israel, who here are Joseph's brethren = spiritual truths, which truths are also from the celestial internal, which is Joseph; or through spiritual good, which is Israel. AC 6553.
Joseph's brethren saw that their father was dead () = things alienated from truth and good...
His brethren also went, and fell down before him () = the submission of those things which are in the Natural. The sons of Israel, who here are the brethren = spiritual truths in the Natural.

In the ancient Churches... they acknowledged all as men of the Church who had lived in the good of charity, and called them brethren, however they might differ in the truths which at this day are called the truths of faith... AC 6705, Explained. NJHD 9.
They who are in self-love call those brethren who love them the most...

(Moses) went out to his brethren () = conjunction with the truths of the Church... As to brethren, they now = the goods, now the truths of the Church; when the celestial Church is treated of they = goods; but when the spiritual Church, truths. The reason is, that the celestial Church is in good, and the spiritual Church in truths, and in ancient times all who were of the Church called each other brethren; they who were of the spiritual Church did indeed call each other brethren from good, but the men of the internal Church did so with a difference according to the quality of the good, thus according to truths, for good has its quality from truths. Afterwards, when the Church turned away from good, and thus also from truth, they no longer called each other brethren from spiritual consanguinity and affinity... but only from natural, and from friendship, and also began to hold it unworthy of them to call one lower than themselves brother... Explained, Illustrated.

As spiritual brotherhood is from love, so that the one belongs to the other, and they who are in good are in the Lord, and the Lord in them (), they are called brethren by the Lord. Illustrated. AC 9338:2.
They did not see a man his brother () = that they did not perceive the truth of any good... Man = truth, and brother good.
Good and truth are as sister and brother.
Hatred against the neighbour is meant by being angry rashly with his brother.
To be reconciled to his brother = charity towards the neighbour.
Brother = good. References.

The conjunction of good and truth is represented in the Word by two married partners, and also by two brothers; by two married partners when the heavenly marriage is treated of... by two brothers when the two ministries of judgment and worship are treated of. Explained. On account of this brotherhood, which is that of the truth belonging to judgment and of the good belonging to worship, Aaron the brother of Moses was chosen to discharge the office of the priesthood. Illustrated.
In the proximate sense, brethren = those who are in the good of charity; and in a sense abstracted from the person, the Lord's brethren = the goods of charity themselves.

Kill ye a man his brother, and a man his companion, and a man his neighbour () = a closing up as to the influx of good and truth, and of things in affinity with them, lest there be any reception and communication... Brother = the good of love and of charity. References. AC 10490:6, Illustrated. AC 10494.
Brother is predicated of good... companion of truth.
I John, who am your brother and companion () = those who are in the good of charity and thence in the truths of faith.

We do not read that the disciples called the Lord brother, because brother = the good which is from the Lord; comparatively as a king calls his relatives brethren, but they do not call him their brother; for the Lord says, One is your Teacher, Christ, but all ye are brethren; Ye call Me Master and Lord, and ye say well, for so I am. AE 746:10.

The Sons of Israel called all brethren who were descended from their father Jacob, and in a wider sense, those also who were descended from Esau; all others, companions. But... in the spiritual sense, by brethren are meant those who are in the good of charity from the Lord, and by companions, those who are in the truths of faith. Illustrated.
Our brethren () = those who are in the doctrine of the New Jerusalem, and in a life according to it.
I am thy fellow-servant and of thy brethren () = that there is nothing Divine in an Angel, but that he is associated with man as a brother with a brother. AR 946.
In the Heavens... those who are higher in rank regard those who are lower as brothers.
Social intercourse in the primitive Church existed among those who called each other brethren in Christ; hence it was the social intercourse of charity, because they were a spiritual brotherhood.

The reason brother () = the good of love, is that in Heaven there are no relationships except spiritual ones, thus no other brotherhoods; for there they do not become brothers from birth, and they who had been brothers in the world do not know each other there, but everyone knows another from the good of love; they who are the most closely conjoined know each other as brothers... Hence it is that in the Word, brother = the good of love. Illustrated.
The brother shall betray the brother to death () = that falsity will destroy good; specifically, that faith alone will destroy charity, for in the Word, faith is called the brother of charity.
Brethren () = all who are in good.

Brethren here () = good and truth, for in the Word these are called brethren; wherefore by Behold how good and pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together is signified that all heavenly good and delight are in the conjunction of good and truth, for they are from it.
To offer a gift upon the altar () = worship from piety, and to be reconciled to one's brother = worship from charity, which is truly worship.

Their fellow-servants and their brethren who shall be killed as they were () = evils, for to kill them is evil. Fellow-servants = those who are in truths, and brethren those who are in goods, and fellow-servants and brethren together = those who are in truths from good.
Asher is blessed above the sons, let him be accepted by his brethren (). Sons = truths, and brethren, the Church from them.
Simeon and Levi the brethren () = faith separated from charity.
A man and a brother who shall be desolated () = faith and charity; a man = the truth of faith, and a brother, the good of charity. AE 633:3.
A strange man not a brother () = a religion which does not agree; also falsity in which there is no good.

Our brethren () = all in the Heavens and all on earth who are in the good of charity; the reason they are called brethren, is that they have one Father, the Lord, and they who are in the good of love to the Lord and in the good of charity towards the neighbour are His sons...
That all who belonged to the Israelitish Church called each other brethren, Illustrated.
That they also called each other a man and a brother; also a companion and a brother, Illustrated. A man and a brother = truth and good, and in the opposite sense, falsity and evil. Illustrated.
That all those are called brethren by the Lord who acknowledge Him, and are in the good of charity from Him. Illustrated.
Brother, here (), means the neighbour in general, thus every man, but specifically him who is in the good of charity and thence in faith from the Lord, whoever he may be.
Of ten brothers in the world five may be in Hell and five in Heaven.
